title: Maharashtra before the Times of Shivaji Maharaj

facts.text: At the beginning of the seventeenth century CE, most of Maharashtra was under Nizamshah of Ahmadnagar and Adilshah of Bijapur.
facts.quote: At the beginning of the seventeenth century CE, most of the territory in Maharashtra was under the control of Nizamshah of Ahmadnagar and Adilshah of Bijapur.

facts.text: The Mughals had entered Khandesh; their objective was to expand their power in the south.
facts.quote: The Mughals had entered Khandesh. Their objective was to expand their power in the south.

facts.text: The Siddi people, who had come from Africa, had settlements along the Konkan coastline.
facts.quote: There were settlements of Siddi people, who had come from Africa, along the coastline of Konkan.

facts.text: The Portuguese had established their rule in Goa and Vasai on the western coastline.
facts.quote: The Portuguese had already established their rule in Goa and Vasai on the western coastline.

facts.text: The British, the Dutch and the French entered through trading companies by setting up factories.
facts.quote: The British, the Dutch and the French had found an entry through the medium of trading companies by setting up factories.

facts.text: People from Europe were called 'Topkar' on the basis of their customary headgear.
facts.quote: These different people from Europe were called 'Topkar' on the basis of their customary headgear.

facts.text: A pargana was made up of many villages; its headquarters was generally called Kasba; a village smaller than a Kasba was called Mauja.
facts.quote: Pargana was made up of many villages. Generally, the headquarters of a pargana was called 'Kasba'. A village smaller than a Kasba was called 'Mauja'.

facts.text: The chief of the village was the Patil; he tried to bring maximum land under cultivation and resolved disputes.
facts.quote: The chief of the village was the Patil. He used to try to bring maximum land under cultivation. When there was any dispute in the village, the Patil resolved it and made peace.

facts.text: A Kulkarni helped the Patil and kept the record of the revenue collected.
facts.quote: A Kulkarni helped the Patil in his work. The Kulkarni kept the record of the revenue that was collected.

facts.text: Baluta was the share of agricultural produce that peasants gave to village artisans for their services.
facts.quote: The peasants gave a share of their agricultural produce to the artisans for the services they rendered to the village community. This share was known as baluta.

facts.text: Indapur kasba of Indapur pargana and Wai kasba of Wai pargana were the headquarters of those parganas.
facts.quote: Indapur kasba of Indapur pargana, Wai kasba of Wai pargana were the headquarters of those parganas.

facts.text: A market (peth) was usually adjacent to a kasba; the Shete and Mahajan were its watandars and the Mahajan maintained its accounts.
facts.quote: There was usually a market (peth) adjacent to a kasba. The Shete and Mahajan were the watandars of the peth. ... The Mahajan maintained the accounts of the peth.

facts.text: A peth established in Pashan near Pune was called Jijapur.
facts.quote: As per the order of Veermata Jajabai, a peth was established in Pashan near Pune. It was called Jijapur.

facts.text: Malpura, Khelpura, Paraspura and Vithapura in Aurangabad were peths named after Maloji, Kheloji, Parasoji and Vithoji.
facts.quote: Malpura, Khelpura, Paraspura, Vithapura, in Aurangabad are also new peths established in the name of Maloji, Kheloji, Parasoji and Vithoji respectively.

facts.text: Shivapur, adjacent to Khed, was a peth established in the name of Shivaji Maharaj.
facts.quote: 'Shivapur' adjacent to 'Khed' was a peth established in the name of Shivaji Maharaj.

facts.text: 'Budruk' is the original town and 'Khurd' the new one, e.g. Vadgaon Budruk and Vadgaon Khurd.
facts.quote: The original town is 'Budruk' and the new one is 'Khurd'. For example, Vadgaon Budruk and Vadgaon Khurd.

facts.text: The Pune pargana was a big pargana of 290 villages.
facts.quote: the Pune pargana was a big pargana. It consisted of 290 villages.

facts.text: There were 64 villages in the Chakan pargana.
facts.quote: There were 64 villages in the Chakan pargana.

facts.text: The Shirwal pargana was small, with only 40 villages.
facts.quote: The Shirwal pargana was small. It had only 40 villages.

facts.text: The Deshmukh and the Deshpande were the watandar officers of the pargana; the Deshmukh was the chief of patils.
facts.quote: The Deshmukh and the Deshpande were the watandar officers of the pargana. The Deshmukh was the chief of patils in a pargana.

facts.text: The Deshpande was the chief of all Kulkarnis in the pargana.
facts.quote: The Deshpande was the chief of all Kulkarnis in the pargana.

facts.text: Vatan is an Arabic word; in Maharashtra it refers to hereditary land for which the holder does not pay revenue.
facts.quote: Vatan is an Arabic word. In Maharashtra, it is used is refer to hereditary land for which the holder does not have to pay revenue.

facts.text: A great famine occurred in Maharashtra in 1630 CE.
facts.quote: A great famine occurred in Maharashtra in 1630 CE.

facts.text: During the famine, people were ready to sell themselves for a piece of bhakri, but nobody would buy them.
facts.quote: 'People were ready to sell themselves for a piece of bhakri, but there was nobody to buy them'.

facts.text: The famine put an end to industries; financial transactions stopped; people wandered far for a livelihood.
facts.quote: The famine put an end to industries. All financial transactions came to a standstill. People had to wander to faraway regions in search of a livelihood.

facts.text: The tradition of Sants in Maharashtra began with Sant Dnyaneshwar and Sant Namdeo.
facts.quote: In Maharashtra, the tradition of Sants which began with Sant Dnyaneshwar and Sant Namdeo was carried on by Sants coming from various strata of the society.

facts.text: Sants from all strata included Sant Chokhamela, Sant Goroba, Sant Sena, Sant Sawata, Sant Narhari and Sant Shaikh Muhammad.
facts.quote: Sant Chokhamela, Sant Goroba, Sant Sena, Sant Sawata, Sant Narhari, Sant Shaikh Muhammad, etc.

facts.text: Women Sants included Soyrabai (Sant Chokhoba's wife), Nirmalabai (his sister), Muktabai, Janabai, Kanhopatra and Bahinabai Siurkar.
facts.quote: Sant Chokhoba's wife Sant Soyrabai, and sister Sant Nirmalabai, Sant Muktabai, Sant Janabai, Sant Kanhopatra, Sant Bahinabai Siurkar and other women were also among them.

facts.text: Pandharpur was the centre of the Sant movement; Vitthal was worshipped there on the banks of the river Chandrabhaga.
facts.quote: Pandharpur was at the centre of the Sant movement. Vitthal was the object of their worship. On the banks of the river Chandrabhaga at Pandharpur...

facts.text: At Pandharpur, equality was propagated through bhajans, keertans and unity meals (kala).
facts.quote: There, equality was propagated through bhajans, keertans, and unity meals (kala).

facts.text: Sant Namdeo was a skilled organiser and performed excellent keertans.
facts.quote: He was a skilled organiser. He performed excellent keertans as well.

facts.text: Sant Namdeo went up to the Punjab; his compositions are included in the 'Guru Granth Sahib' of the Sikhs.
facts.quote: He went up to the Punjab, propagating his thoughts. His compositions are included in the 'Guru Granth Sahib' of Sikhs.

facts.text: Sant Namdeo built a memorial to Sant Chokhamela at Pandharpur.
facts.quote: He built a memorial to Sant Chokhamela at Pandharpur.

facts.text: Sant Dnyaneshwar wrote the 'Bhavartha-deepika' or 'Dnyaneshwari', explaining the Bhagavad Geeta, and also composed the 'Amrutanubhav'.
facts.quote: He wrote the 'Bhavartha-deepika' or 'Dnyaneshwari' which elucidates the meaning of the Sanskrit 'Bhagavad Geeta'. He also composed the 'Amrutanubhav'.

facts.text: Sant Dnyaneshwar gave the prestige of a religion to the Varkari movement; his 'Pasayadaan' is in the Dnyaneshwari.
facts.quote: He gave the prestige of a religion to the Varkari movement. ... His 'Pasayadaan' in Dnyaneshwari uplifts the mind.

facts.text: Sant Dnyaneshwar's brothers were Sant Nivruttinath and Sant Sopandev, and his sister was Muktabai.
facts.quote: The poetic compositions of his brothers Sant Nivruttinath and Sant Sopandev and sister Muktabai are well-known.

facts.text: Sant Eknath's compositions include abhanga, gavalana and bharud.
facts.quote: His compositions are many and diverse. They include abhanga, gavalana, bharud, etc.

facts.text: Sant Eknath portrayed people's life in the Bhavarth Ramayana and explained in Marathi the Bhakti part of the Sanskrit 'Bhagwat'.
facts.quote: He has portrayed people's life in Bhavarth Ramayana through the story of Ram. He explained in Marathi, the Bhakti part of the Sanskrit work 'Bhagwat'.

facts.text: Sant Eknath believed Marathi was inferior to no other language and criticised those who hated other religions.
facts.quote: He believed that our Marathi language was inferior to no other language. ... He heavily criticised those who hated other religions.

facts.text: Sant Tukaram belonged to Dehu near Pune; his 'Gatha' is a precious treasure of the Marathi language.
facts.quote: He belonged to Dehu near Pune. ... His 'Gatha' is a precious treasure of the Marathi language.

facts.text: Sant Tukaram threw the loan documents into the river Indrayani and freed many poor families from debt.
facts.quote: he threw in the river Indrayani, the documents of the loans that people had borrowed from him and freed many poor families from the bonds of loan.

facts.text: Sant Tukaram stressed that devotion should be coupled with morality; dogmatic people sank his abhangas in the Indrayani.
facts.quote: He stressed that devotion (Bhakti) should be coupled with morality. ... Some dogmatic people opposed the social awakening that he had undertaken, and sank his abhangas in the Indrayani.

facts.text: Sant Tukaram's disciples and associates included Navji Mali, Gavnarshet Wani, Santaji Jagnade, Shivba Kasar, Bahinabai Siurkar and Mahadajipant Kulkarni.
facts.quote: They include Navji Mali, Gavnarshet Wani, Santaji Jagnade, Shivba Kasar, Bahinabai Siurkar and Mahadajipant Kulkarni.

facts.text: Gangarampant Maval and Santaji Jagnade wrote down the abhangas of Sant Tukaram.
facts.quote: An important task completed by Gangarampant Maval and Santaji Jagnade was writing down the abhangas of Sant Tukaram.

facts.text: The Sants explained the complex dharma of the scholars (Shastris and Pandits) in the language of the people.
facts.quote: The Sants elucidated the complex dharma of the scholars (Shastris and Pandits) in the language of the people.

facts.text: The Sants found God in their work; Sant Sawata's famous line refers to farm work.
facts.quote: They found God in their work. Sant Sawata said, ... This statement refers to farm work but applies to work in all walks of life.

facts.text: Ramdas Swami was from Jamb in Marathwada and explained the importance of physical fitness.
facts.quote: Ramdas Swami : He was from Jamb in Marathwada. He explained the importance of physical fitness to the people

facts.text: Ramdas Swami gave lessons through Dasbodh, Karunashtaka and Manache Shlok.
facts.quote: He gave practical education and lessons in good conduct through his works like Dasbodh, Karunashtaka, Manache Shlok.

facts.text: Ramdas Swami founded the Samarth Sampradaya, with Chaphal as its centre, and propagated the worship of Ram and Hanuman.
facts.quote: founded the Samarth Sampradaya. Chaphal was the centre of this Sampradaya. He propagated the worship of Ram and Hanuman.

facts.text: Shahaji Maharaj, considered a visionary of Swaraj, was at the forefront of those dreaming of freedom.
facts.quote: Among them, Shahaji Maharaj, who is considered to be a visionary of Swaraj was on the forefront.
